hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the price per $1$ acre.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{total price}}}{\maroonD{\text{acres}}} = \purpleD{\text{price per acre}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want, not the order of the columns in the original table.

Plot| $\blueE{\text{Price}} $ || $\maroonD{\text{Area (acres)}}$||$\purpleE{\text{Price per acre}}$ 
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Bumper Crop |$89{,}000$|$\div$ | $22$|$\approx$|$4{,}045$
Pay Dirt|$312{,}000$ |$\div$ |$88$ | $\approx$|$3{,}545$
The Corn-er Lot |$390{,}000$ |$\div$ | $99$|$\approx$| $3{,}939$

###Comparing the unit rates

Plot | Thousands| Hundreds | Tens | Ones
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Bumper Crop | $4$ | $0$ | $4$ | $5$
Pay Dirt| $\redE{3}$ | $\redE{5}$ | $4$ | $5$
The Corn-er Lot | $\redE{3}$ | $9$ | $3$ | $9$

Pay Dirt and the Corn-er Lot both cost $3$ thousands of dollars per acre, but between those two, Pay Dirt costs the least hundreds of dollars per acre.

###Conclusion

Pay Dirt has the lowest price per acre.

question.content:
Three plots of farmland are for sale.  Each plot is a different size.

Plot  | Area (in acres)| Price (in dollars)
- | :-: | :-:
Bumper Crop | $22$| $89{,}000$ 
Pay Dirt | $88$ | $312{,}000$
The Corn-er Lot  | $99$| $390{,}000$

**Which plot of farmland has the lowest *price per acre*?**
